notable_absence.finding: Round 8's Capella twin for this page (cloud/eventing/eventing-handler-advancedInsertOp.json) was flagged by verify-evidence.py for an unquotable relation: `eventing:lcb-key-eexists-error behavesDifferentlyUnder eventing:cas-conditioned-delete`, evidenced only by the bare error-object JSON, which does not textually support a 'behaves differently under' claim. The Server page makes the analogous underlying claim (the same LCB_KEY_EEXISTS name/code overloaded across two distinct conditions), so this record deliberately does NOT reuse that flagged relation. Instead: this page's LCB_KEY_EEXISTS fires on a duplicate-key INSERT (`"key_already_exists": true`, desc 'The document key already exists in the server.'), while advancedReplaceOp.md/advancedDeleteOp.md's LCB_KEY_EEXISTS fires on a CAS mismatch (`"cas_mismatch": true`, desc 'The document key exists with a CAS value different than specified') - same error identifier, two genuinely different documented conditions, distinguished only by an extra boolean sub-flag and a different desc string. No existing predicate in the registry cleanly expresses 'one error code is overloaded for two distinct conditions', so this is recorded here as a finding rather than forced into a relation - worth a docs-issue and worth the coordinator's attention when reconciling eventing:lcb-key-eexists-error.
